open-question.question: Does the task-list tool require the fixed first-line heading of each task file it writes to (# TASKS TODO or # TASKS DONE), refusing with one Error: line a file whose first line is anything else, or does it treat whatever stands before the first ## section as opaque content that it carries through unchanged and never checks?
open-question.alternative: Before any insert, append, or move, the tool checks that the first line of each task file it is about to write is exactly its fixed heading (# TASKS TODO for TASKS_TODO.md, # TASKS DONE for TASKS_DONE.md). Any other first line, an empty file included, is refused with one Error: line naming the file, and both files stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Anything else standing between that heading and the first ## section is carried through unchanged and never checked. Initialize keeps its recorded behaviour of replacing TASKS_TODO.md whole, writing the heading itself, so it does not check the old first line. It catches a file that is not a task file at all, such as a truncated, overwritten, or hand-mangled one, before the tool splices sections into it. It costs nothing today, since all 92 task files in the repository's 46 milestone directories start with exactly the heading define_milestone.py writes, and it still leaves any note a person adds under the heading alone. The tool picks both paths itself from MILESTONE_DIR, so a swapped or wrong file can only come from a hand edit, and the check mostly guards a case that never occurs. It also makes a cosmetic edit to the heading line, like a changed case or a trailing word, a hard stop for every completion, submission, and append until someone repairs the line by hand. It adds one more refusal path that needs its own tests.

The tool checks the whole preamble, not just its first line, before any insert, append, or move. Everything before the first ## section must be exactly the fixed heading for that file followed by nothing but blank lines. A different first line, an empty file, or any other text in the preamble is refused with one Error: line and both files left byte-for-byte unchanged. Initialize keeps replacing TASKS_TODO.md whole and checks nothing. The files keep exactly the shape define_milestone.py creates and the task format describes, so no text outside a ## section can slip in unnoticed. The tool's own parser never has to decide what non-section text before the first heading means. A note a person adds under the heading, which is harmless to every reader of the files, blocks every write to that file until it is removed by hand. That makes it the strictest option and the one most likely to stop a headless completion chain over a cosmetic detail. The preamble is also checked by a rule that nothing else in the workflow states or needs.

The tool never checks the heading. Whatever stands before the first ## section in a task file, whether the fixed heading, other text, or nothing at all, is treated as opaque content and carried through byte-for-byte on every insert, append, and move. Initialize keeps its recorded behaviour of replacing TASKS_TODO.md whole with the fixed heading followed by the list. It adds no refusal path and no rule beyond the ## and --- sections the tool actually works on. A hand edit above the first section never blocks a completion or a submission, and the tool's job stays limited to the sections it moves and inserts, which is all the decisions recorded so far define. A task file whose top has been damaged or replaced is written into without complaint, so the corruption carries forward silently until a person or a reading skill notices it. The fixed heading becomes a convention that only define_milestone.py and initialize enforce, and the first-line contract nothing else checks drifts with every hand edit.

The tool never refuses over the preamble and never checks it. On every write to a task file it discards whatever stands before the first ## section and writes the fixed heading for that file plus one blank line in its place, so every file the tool has touched starts with the canonical preamble. Initialize does the same for TASKS_TODO.md as part of its whole-file replacement. The files heal themselves: a damaged, missing, or altered heading is corrected on the next write and never blocks a run, and the task files converge on the shape define_milestone.py creates without anyone having to repair them by hand. Any text a person put above the first section is silently dropped on the next completion or submission, with nothing printed, and only the commit diff shows it, which is the silent loss the tool's contract otherwise avoids. Whether rewriting bytes outside the section being written fits depends on the whole-file-rewrite-or-splice axis owned by a sibling question.

The tool never refuses over the preamble. On every write to a task file it makes sure the first line is the fixed heading for that file. If the first line is a single-# heading with different text, the tool replaces it with the fixed heading. If the file starts with anything else, such as a ## section, plain text, or nothing, the tool inserts the fixed heading and a blank line above it. Any other preamble text is carried through unchanged. A missing or altered heading is repaired without ever blocking a run, and unlike rewriting the whole preamble it keeps any note a person added under the heading. It needs a repair rule (replace or insert) that is more complex than either checking the heading or ignoring it, and that rule has to be tested. It still rewrites a line outside the section being written without saying so, which depends on the whole-file-rewrite-or-splice axis owned by a sibling question. A file that is not a task file at all gets a heading added on top of it instead of being refused.
